title: Graduating Student — Work, Visa & Tax Next Steps
intro: For students approaching graduation and planning what's next (work authorization, status, taxes). These are high-stakes and time-sensitive — confirm every date with your DSO.

items.text: You can apply for up to 12 months of post-completion OPT related to your major. Request a DSO recommendation, then file Form I-765 for the EAD within the required window tied to your program end date.
On post-completion OPT you may not accrue more than 90 days of unemployment — track it carefully.
A qualifying STEM degree can get a one-time 24-month extension. You'll need an E-Verify employer and a signed Form I-983 training plan.
The STEM extension adds 60 more days of allowed unemployment (150 total across OPT).
Your residency status can change as your years in the U.S. add up (the 5-year exempt rule), which changes which return you file.
Watch for a Form 1042-S (e.g. treaty-exempt wages or taxable scholarship) in addition to any W-2 when you file.
OPT/CPT wages stay FICA-exempt only while you remain a nonresident alien; once you become a resident alien, FICA applies.
Report employer and address changes to your DSO promptly (especially on OPT/STEM OPT) to stay in status.
Plan early — OPT processing takes time, so start the DSO conversation months before you graduate.
